review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the related definitions in TauCeti (normalSubspace, normalTube) and in Mathlib (Complex.isometryOfOrthonormal, Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI). I did not flag boundaryInclusion. The file proves it is an embedding and gives its range, but I found no existing bundled interface that would be clearly better for it. exteriorFrontierHomeomorph is already a Homeomorph. IsSolidTorusNeighborhood is an intended predicate structure. The one finding is exists_normalDisc, whose fibrewise ψ z is a bare function with separately stated linear-isometry properties. I did not check whether bundling is compatible with the continuity statement. The suggested bundled form keeps the joint-continuity field as an unbundled function.

findings.problem: The docstring says ψ z is a family of linear isometries from ℂ onto the normal plane. The statement exposes ψ z only as a bare function ℂ → ℝ³. It records the isometry, injectivity, range and onto-the-normal-plane properties as four separate hypotheses. Linearity is not stated, even though ψ z w = re w • n₁ z + im w • n₂ z is ℝ-linear. Injectivity is redundant, since it follows from the norm identity once ψ z is linear. The consumer `exists_isSolidTorusNeighborhood` re-derives norm facts by hand (`hnorm` uses `(hψ q.2).2.1`) and pulls injectivity out as `(hψ _).2.2.1`.
findings.proposed_change: State the result with a bundled map, for example `∃ ψ : Circle → ℂ →ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³, Continuous (fun q : SolidTorus => ψ q.2 q.1) ∧ ∀ z, (∀ w, ψ z w ∈ normalSubspace (𝓡 1) f z) ∧ ∀ v ∈ normalSubspace (𝓡 1) f z, ∃ w, ψ z w = v`. Equivalently, say `LinearMap.range (ψ z).toLinearMap = normalSubspace (𝓡 1) f z`. Build `ψ z` from the frame, for instance as the linear isometry that sends the basis `1, I` to `n₁ z, n₂ z`. The `Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI` / `Complex.isometryOfOrthonormal` API is the natural route. The norm identity then follows from `LinearIsometry.norm_map`, and injectivity from `LinearIsometry.injective`. The uses of `(hψ z).2.1` and `(hψ _).2.2.1` in `exists_isSolidTorusNeighborhood` become `(ψ z).norm_map` and `(ψ z).injective`. The manual `sq_eq_sq₀` / `normSq_apply` / `Complex.ext` computations in the proof of this lemma are replaced by one construction of the isometry. Only the continuity statement stays about the unbundled function `fun q => ψ q.2 q.1`.
findings.benefit: The statement matches its docstring and the geometric meaning, a linear isometry from ℂ onto the normal plane. The redundant injectivity field and the hand-written norm identities go away. Callers get the existing `LinearIsometry` API (`norm_map`, `injective`, `range`, composition with scalar multiplication) instead of re-deriving it.
